the wall (Jerusalem) He remembers against the wall of the sea. When confusion has been decreed as punishment for man and beast, He remembers the loud entreaty of the earth. As it was written through Thy prophet:
הבן
'Is Ephraim a dear son to me, or a delightful child that whenever I speak of him, I still remember him? Accordingly, my love for him is aroused, I shall surely have compassion on him, says the Lord'.
אלהינו

Our God and God of our fathers, remember us with a good remembrance before Thee and consider us with salvation and compassion from the ancient heavens and remember on our behalf, O Lord our God, the covenant and the grace and the oath which Thou hast sworn to our father Abraham on Mount Moriah and let there appear before Thee the scene when Abraham our father bound his son Isaac on the altar and subdued his compassion in order to do Thy will with a whole heart. Thus let.Thy compassion subdue Thy wrath from upon us and in Thy great goodness let the fury of Thine anger turn back from Thy people, Thy city and Thine inheritance. Fulfil for us, O Lord our God, the word that Thou
uncertainties: 'let.Thy': a stray dot or period is printed between the words. I kept it as printed.

blocks.text: היום

On this day the world was completed. On this day He brings to judgment all the world's creatures, either like children or like slaves. If like children, then have mercy upon us as a father has mercy on children. If like slaves, then our eyes are lifted to Thee until Thou wilt be gracious to us and make our verdict shine forth like light, O Awe-inspiring and Holy One.
uncertainties: Removed the line-wrap hyphen in chil-dren. Kept the real hyphen in Awe-inspiring. The English has no speaker label to match קר״ח.

blocks.text: ארשת

May the utterance of our lips be pleasing before Thee, O lofty and exalted God, who understands and listens, pays heed and hearkens to the sound of (the memory of) our Tekiah. Mayest Thou accept with compassion and favour the order of our verses of remembrance.
uncertainties: '(the memory of)' matches the Shabbat cue, but the English gives no Shabbat label.

blocks.text: אתה

Thou hast revealed Thyself in the cloud of Thy glory to Thy holy people in order to speak with them, from heaven hast Thou made Thy voice heard to them and in clouds of purity hast Thou revealed Thyself to them. The whole world trembled before Thee and the creatures of the creation were in awe of Thee when Thou didst reveal Thyself, O our King, on Mount Sinai in order to teach Thy people Torah and commandment. Thou didst make them hear the majesty of Thy voice and Thy holy words out of fiery flames. With thunder and lightning didst Thou reveal Thyself to them and with the sound of the Shofar didst Thou appear to them.
uncertainties: The English does not render the variant (כָּל).

notes: I read only the 18 listed images (s288–s293 and their enlargements). I did not see s276, so I can't independently confirm its instructions about Shabbat/weekday placement or the later reader repeat. I have not removed or assumed anything from them.

Weekday/Shabbat continuity: on s288/289 a horizontal rule splits the page, weekday on top and Shabbat below. On s290/291 the split turns vertical (two columns). On the Hebrew page weekday is on the right and Shabbat on the left; the English page mirrors this. Both threads end with the shared full-width verse הֲבֵן יַקִּיר / 'Is Ephraim…', after which the full-width body resumes.

Weekday thread: s288 top → s290 right column → shared הֲבֵן. Shabbat thread: s288 bottom (ending תִּעַבְתָּ…מֵהֶם.) → s290 left column (עֵדוּת לְזִכָּרוֹן:) → כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ → shared הֲבֵן.
